messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — got a list of field asks from two customers asking for stronger guidance from the Optimize toolkit. They want: 1) per-model quantization recs, 2) adaptive batching defaults, 3) eval-triggered alerts for quality regressions. Need to prioritize and produce gating criteria for pilot.
Trent Alvarez: thanks. can we get specifics on expected latency p99 and token-rate for their workloads? those drive batching/quantization tradeoffs.
Maya Chen: brief: acmehealth wants p99 < 150ms for short chat (<256 tokens) at ~40 qps. betafin wants cost reductions -> willing to accept p99 up to 300ms for longer contexts (~1024) at 10 qps.
Sofia Patel: sounds like two different personas. proposal: split pilot lanes — latency-sensitive (default: aggressive caching + small batches) vs cost-sensitive (default: higher quant + larger batch heuristics).
Alex R.: for launch gates we should require: - measurable end-to-end SLOs on both lanes, - docs for SDK flags to opt into heuristics, - canary rollout plan with auto-fallback to baseline model.
Jonah (prod): +1. Also require eval-trigger config: a thresholded metric (e.g., rouge/EM drop or hallucination spike) that fires an alert and auto-rolls back to previous candidate model. need UX in console for customers to view failing prompt sets.
Trent Alvarez: implementation notes: quant recs should be profile-driven. runtime can test per-model mixed-quant options on a small sample and emit recommended profiles: {"fp16": "baseline", "4bit-qat": "safe", "4bit-llm": "experimental"}. keep heuristics as opt-in defaults.
Maya Chen: customers asked for a simple decision tree they can follow — we should produce a one-page "quickstart recs" for each lane and a checklist for pilot acceptance.
Sofia Patel: prioritization: 1) eval-triggered alerts (safety/regression risk), 2) latency lane defaults + docs, 3) cost lane quant profiles + autobatch heuristics. rationale: alerts reduce risk fastest.
Alex R.: agree. Acceptance criteria draft: - Alerts: configurable rule + alert delivery (email + console) + auto-rollbacks tested in staging. - Latency lane: default config yields <=150ms p99 for 90% of short-chat tests. - Cost lane: >=25% token-cost reduction vs baseline for 80% of sampled prompts without >5% quality degradation.
Jonah (prod): can ops-bot run a quick synthetic to validate rollback path? ops-bot: Deploy check scheduled: run synthetic pilot harness in staging at 18:00 UTC, will attempt rollback if error rate > 2%.
ops-bot: Scheduled synthetic test job created: job_id=opt-toolkit-pilot-202403, eta=2024-04-17T18:00:00Z.
Maya Chen: perfect. next steps: - Trent + infra to scope profiling job and quant pipelines, - Sofia + product to write one-pagers and gating doc, - Jonah to own eval-alert UX + canary plan. sync tomorrow 10am.
Trent Alvarez: i'm going to prototype per-model microbenchmarks and share results by EOD.
Sofia Patel: i'll draft the gating checklist and post a PR to the docs repo.
Alex R.: I'll sketch the rollback playbook and failure-mode matrix.
Jonah (prod): I'll mock the console view for failing prompt sets and wireframes for alert thresholds.
Maya Chen: thanks team — keeping this tight since two customers are in pilot window. :thumbsup:
